owner_basis: Owner routing update 2026-11-01 (via main): update dispatch routing per the Swarm definition (all provider endpoints participating in 3L0 DoE) + the no-hard-select principle so the scoring planes (3L0, DoE, MoneyBall, MVT/ATES) are POPULATED — every routed+assigned dispatch emits its full stamp {task class, arm/provider, model, run id, outcome, quota/cost class} to each plane's intake, not just the desk-feed.
hypothesis: When every routed dispatch emits its full stamp to every scoring plane's intake at completion, the planes' scoring populations grow from live work across all arms (comparative signal per instance_key), replacing the single-outcome starvation recorded by the 3L0 plane (one distinct outcome event, #1424).

design.units: Every routed+assigned dispatch completed by the fleet routing layer (workflow runs, provider dispatches, cert units) — the continuous production flow itself; no synthetic units.
design.factor: The resolved arm (provider x configured instance) as stamped post-hoc by the routing layer; dispatch is route-parameterized and records never carry a pre-pinned model as their result.
design.assignment: The routing layer assigns across arms by task-fit rotation/tranches (no hard-select, swarm doc section 20); single-arm routing only as a recorded constrained arm.
responses: gate_call / confirmed where the instance made a call
usage slots where the provider returns them (schema rev 1.1; value null unless measured/estimated)
design.sha_convention: baseline_sha = the master tip the dispatch started from; candidate_sha = the resulting ref for build dispatches (PR head / merge), else the master tip at completion. Both are real repo refs the arm's work was scored against; the convention is declared here, never dressed as a designed A/B comparison.
design.honesty: Routed production dispatches are OBSERVATIONAL population for the planes unless they belong to a designed campaign's sets; records carry their real status and cohort and are never retro-dressed as designed arms (MVT/ATES intake honesty rules). Missing fields are null / NOT_ESTABLISHED, never invented.

emits: ops/moneyball/routed-dispatch/*.json (moneyball-plane/v2 score records, one per dispatch; deterministic rubric in the emitter, weights fixed at this intake, quantities null = unidentified; the plane validates on master)
experiments/doe/routed-dispatch/stamps/*.json (canonical stamp retention — backfill doctrine: full history re-derivable at every scoring version change; records immutable, versions re-derive scores)
automation.identity: Records carry instance_key where the dispatch stamp provides the configured-instance tuple (scripts/doe/instance_key.py); stamps without the tuple group by provider/model and are marked NOT_ESTABLISHED at the instance level.

moneyball_backfill.doctrine: owner backfill doctrine (2026-11-01, canonical record: DoE expert); MoneyBall addendum via the plane: at every scoring version change the feed backfills - prior records re-scored under the new version, audited + improved, version results compared continuously as per-entity version pairs until DoE culling retires a version
moneyball_backfill.hooks: records carry schema per record (moneyball-plane/v2); backfilled record = NEW record per entity under the new schema at ops/moneyball/routed-dispatch/<dispatch_id>--<schema-slug>.json with record_id mb-<dispatch_id>--<schema-slug> and a supersedes ref to the prior record_id; live records keep record_id mb-<dispatch_id>; re-scoring source = the retained canonical stamps (experiments/doe/routed-dispatch/stamps/); the plane validates backfilled records identically and verdicts note version pairs
